rules.reason: The decompiler placed IButtonWindow() around addEventListener's Void return. Restore the cast of findChildByName before registering the original callback.
Normalize JSONEncoder's describeType descendant predicate onto a named XMLList compatibility operation; ax3 cannot parse E4X wildcard predicates.
Normalize JSONEncoder's E4X metadata attribute predicate onto the XMLList compatibility API; ax3 cannot parse dot-parenthesized E4X predicates.
Capabilities.version.split returns an untyped AS3 Array. Its second element is the version string; make the implicit AS3 String coercion explicit before split.

The decompiler left an assignment and second break after the CAMERA_SHUTTER case's unconditional break. Those statements are unreachable in the authoritative AS3 and Haxe correctly rejects the stray retained break; remove only that dead tail.
AS3 var declarations are function-scoped. TraxSample.setSample declares two write indexes inside its first branch and reuses them in later branches.
AS3 var declarations are function-scoped. TraxSample.addSample likewise reuses three indexes outside the branches where the decompiler wrote them.
Companion to the two TraxSample function-scope hoists: retain the original assignment sites without redeclaring their variables in Haxe block scope.
The decompiler copied the minimize callback into the notification-button cleanup. Restore the callback paired with that button's addEventListener.
The decompiler lost removeEventListener at the stream-button cleanup call. Restore the inverse of its constructor registration.
Both conditional switch exits are at the end of previewImage; returning skips exactly the remaining case body without breaking a nonexistent Haxe loop.
AS3's block-local glyph declaration is function-scoped and reused in the later loop; hoist without changing its assignment.
Companion to the function-scope declaration hoist; keep the original lookup at its original execution site.
This continue targets the immediately enclosing for loop, even inside the switch; the AS3 label is redundant and ax3 cannot parse it.
Window error diagnostics must use the existing HTML5 Logger adapter instead of pulling in the AS3 Habbo application root just for trackLoginStep.
the one E4X predicate in core is normalized to an explicit compatibility method. The clean-client source remains untouched; ax3 and Haxe have no native `.(@attribute == value)` syntax
ax3 cannot lex XML literals. Preserve the complete script/CDATA bytes in a quoted `new XML(...)` value; the transformation JSON-escapes the capture
Haxe has no finally. These measured single-cleanup sites contain no return/break/continue, so duplicating cleanup on normal and exceptional exits is semantics-preserving and count-guarded
AS3 `var` is function-scoped but Haxe `var` is block-scoped. Normalize the one load-bearing core site by declaring it before the loop and assigning inside
rules.pattern: (?m)^([ \t]*)for \(var i:uint; i < this\._fileLoadQueue\.length; i\+\+\)\s*\n\1\{\s*\n\1    var assetLibrary:IAssetLibrary =

rules.reason: AS3 permits `super()` in a class with no explicit base, meaning Object. Haxe has no callable implicit Object constructor, so those calls must be omitted; classes with an explicit `extends` clause are deliberately excluded
AS3 \b has no Haxe spelling; \x08 is the same character
AS3 \f has no Haxe spelling; \x0C is the same character
AS3 \v has no Haxe spelling; \x0B is the same character
ax3 requires each switch case to end in a terminal expression. `parseError` always throws, so the trailing return is unreachable and changes no behaviour

AS3 `var` is function-scoped, so a later `for (index = 0; ...)` reuses a counter declared by an earlier loop in the same function. Haxe scopes per block, so the bare reuse is an unknown identifier. Each Haxe loop gets its own scope, so re-declaring is equivalent

AS3 `Map` extends flash.utils.Proxy, so `map[key]` routes through its getProperty. SkyHaxe's Map is a documented seam that exposes those reads as getValue/setValue instead, and ax3 emits the array access verbatim -- which compiles to a plain JS property read and always yields null. Scoped to MapStuffData because IntArrayStuffData and StringArrayStuffData index a real Array with the same field name, and rewriting those would be wrong
AS3 String.charCodeAt() defaults its index to 0; Haxe's requires one, so the converted call is a compile error. Making the implicit 0 explicit preserves the AS3 semantics exactly

ax3 types an untyped Array's `indexOf` as Dynamic, so adding it to an int is a 'Dynamic + operation'. AS3 `Array.indexOf` returns int; making that explicit preserves the original type rather than changing behaviour
the child element is called `elements`, colliding with XML's elements() method
`list[0].@value` -- the index erases the XML type the attribute read needs
`list[0].@frames` -- the index erases the XML type the attribute read needs
restore the bitwise AND the ARGB composition needs
E4X literals whose attribute values are {expressions}; ax3 can lex neither the literal nor the interpolation

HabboMain's nested startup config is one of only three E4X literals in the source corpus with expression-valued attributes. Express the same XML document as an AS3 XML constructor so ax3 can parse the executable owner.
rules.replacement: new XML((("<config><asset-libraries><library url=\"" + assetBase + "hh_human_body.swf\"/><library url=\"" + assetBase + "hh_human_item.swf\"/></asset-libraries><service-libraries/><component-libraries/></config>")))

rules.reason: the avatar package's hardcoded XML fallbacks; ax3 has no E4X literal syntax

same missing terminator, on a field rather than a local: GeometryType's last constant has no semicolon, so the closing brace of the class parses as part of the declaration. Restricted to string-literal initializers, where nothing can be continued onto the next line

ax3 loses E4X typing after XMLList[0], so the following `.part` is emitted as a Haxe field instead of the equivalent child query. Spell the child call explicitly in the staged copy; the authoritative AS3 remains untouched
AS3 applies ToNumber when an XML attribute is compared with a number. ax3 types attribute access as String for assignment compatibility; make this one numeric comparison explicit in the staged source
case CLICK falls into default, so a click also runs the base mouseEvent
InfoStandFurniView's save-branding case falls through to use when the user is not staff. Haxe has no switch fall-through, so make the two outcomes explicit while retaining the shared terminal break.
Flash TextFormat exposes nullable Object-valued margins. This arithmetic site relies on AS3 int(null)==0; make those coercions explicit so the generated Haxe retains the same numeric calculation.
TextField.allowedDomains is an AIR application-sandbox extension and has no HTML5 equivalent. Browser image access is governed by CORS, so omit this guarded AIR-only assignment from generated Haxe.
rules.pattern: (?ms)\s*// Whitelist the image hosts.*?\n\s*if \(\("allowedDomains" in _field\)\)\s*\{\s*_field\["allowedDomains"\] = new <String>\[.*?\];\s*\}

rules.reason: AS3 uses conditional break statements to select the one visible infostand view before leaving the switch. Haxe switches do not accept break; an if/else-if chain preserves that single-view choice.
AS3's two guard breaks leave the REPORT switch case. Express the same guard positively because Haxe switch cases terminate without break.
ax3 mis-parses a braceless else whose body is `delete`, silently dropping the file
join() over a mixed array literal: Haxe cannot type it, concatenation is the same string
int/String ternary in a debug dump; Haxe needs both branches to agree
rotationX is Flash 3D; OpenFL has no such property and nothing to preserve
Function.apply on a super method; Haxe has no closure for one
Function.apply on a super method; Haxe has no closure for one
POSTURE_LAY falls through WALK (sets _actionsSorted) and STAND (sets it again) into the addActionData tail. Give it that tail directly
and WALK and STAND each fall through to the same tail
Haxe has one namespace per type; AS3 has two, and Vector3D uses both for the same three names

FZip decides at class-init whether the running Flash Player's ByteArray has uncompress(algorithm) and inflate(), by reading describeType() output with an E4X predicate. Both are always present on the port's ByteArray, so the answer is a constant -- and the predicate is E4X ax3 cannot parse. FZip itself is unreachable from SkyHaxe, which reads SWFs with its own SwfFile, but it is in the closure because AvatarAssetDownloadLibrary reaches LibraryLoader

the same pattern one switch out: EFFECT conditionally sets _actionsSorted and then falls through DANCE, TALK and the expressions into their shared addActionData tail. Note this tail takes both arguments, unlike the posture one
decompiled output leaves some declarations unterminated; ax3 has no automatic-semicolon-insertion, so `var content:ByteArray` fails to parse
same artefact for a call statement; only rewritten when the next line clearly starts a new statement, so a wrapped argument list is never joined
Haxe supplies Vector; the AS3 `__AS3__.vec` imports do not resolve
OpenFL has no MorphShape display class on HTML5. Window GraphicContext only constructs it as a drawable shape container, so the supported Shape class provides the same surface used by this client.

QName only reaches these branches as Flash Proxy's property token. Generated Haxe has no Proxy dispatch and passes map keys explicitly, so remove the two unreachable QName normalization blocks rather than inventing a QName class.

Flash Proxy has no OpenFL target class. The generated methods are made public by the companion proxy rule, so these collection wrappers can use their ordinary concrete methods without inheriting the Flash interception base.
ax3 cannot parse `use namespace`. The Proxy members it scopes become public instead, which is what the publicise-proxy-overrides rule below does
the namespace import is dead once the directive is gone
these members were flash_proxy-scoped; after dropping Flash's unavailable Proxy base they become ordinary public Haxe methods, not overrides
decompiler artefact: `import a.b.C; C;` leaves a bare expression statement after the import, which ax3 reads as a namespace access
two Component callbacks are immediately invoked function expressions nested inside another call. Haxe requires the function expression parenthesized
close the two explicit IIFE parentheses inserted by wrap-component-iife-open

assignment half of hoist-function-scoped-library-loader-declare

rules.pattern: (?m)^([ \t]*)for each \(var loader:LibraryLoader in this\._loaders\)(?=[\s\S]{0,300}for each \(loader in this\._queue\))$

rules.reason: decompiled `for (type in map)` drops the declaration AS3 requires; ax3 reads the loop variable as an undefined identifier. `for each` is left alone -- it has its own handling
decompiler artefact: an empty statement immediately after a block opener
AS3 permits inherited property access as `super.message`; Haxe only permits methods through super. `this.message` resolves the same inherited Error value
the SWC Error base owns toString although the decompiled client omitted the AS3 override modifier; Haxe requires it explicitly on the ASError boundary
ax3 cannot parse the labelled for-each; an explicit match flag preserves continue-to-outer-loop behavior.

(?ms)            loop0:?
            for each \(item in this\._widget\.items\)?

                    \{?
                        continue;?

                    continue loop0;?
                \}

rules.reason: Qualify the four Graphics calls explicitly; this is the exact AS3 with-block receiver and ax3 has no with statement.
Restore two semicolons omitted by the decompiler so the original imports parse.
